rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and representation; project retained. As the earlier ruling on this line: Form 8814, Form 4972 and the other line 16 amounts are refused through scope.other_line16, and the second selects the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet by line 3a or QDCG line 3 more than zero, which agrees with the project's guard (Schedule D line 17, or capital gain distributions when no Schedule D is needed). The only change from that response is that the second writes Schedule D line 17 out as lines 15 and 16 both above zero, which is sd.line17's definition (f1040sd p. 2, line 17, "Are lines 15 and 16 both gains?"). Both apply i1040sd p. 15, "Don’t use the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet or this worksheet to figure your tax if: Line 15 or line 16 of Schedule D is zero or less and you have no qualified dividends on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 3a; or Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 15, is zero or less".

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and equivalent; project retained (as the earlier rulings on this line, which this response combines). Form 8814, Form 4972 and the other line 16 amounts are refused through scope.other_line16, as the second's note says. The second selects the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet by line 3a or QDCG line 3 above zero, which agrees with the project's guard (Schedule D line 17, or capital gain distributions when no Schedule D is needed); it selects the Schedule D Tax Worksheet by Schedule D line 17 Yes with line 20 No (sd.line20 false, which includes every Form 4952 filer) or Form 4952 line 4g above zero, where the project takes the worksheet's own condition for Form 4952 filers (amb.2025.sd4952_selection). i1040sd p. 15, Schedule D Tax Worksheet, "Don't use the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet or this worksheet to figure your tax if: Line 15 or line 16 of Schedule D is zero or less and you have no qualified dividends on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 3a; or Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 15, is zero or less". The difference changes no tax: with line 4g and Schedule D lines 18 and 19 zero the Schedule D Tax Worksheet reduces to the other worksheet (the earlier ruling's evaluation of 233 returns found no difference). The ordinary branch (Tax Table below the boundary, Tax Computation Worksheet above) is the same on both sides. No change to the data.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Both use the Schedule D Tax Worksheet when Schedule D lines 15 and 16 are gains with line 18 or 19 more than zero, or Form 4952 line 4g is more than zero, and the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet otherwise. The project also applies the worksheet's exceptions (i1040sd p. 15: 'Don't use the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet or this worksheet to figure your tax if: Line 15 or line 16 of Schedule D is zero or less and you have no qualified dividends on Form 1040 ... line 3a; or Form 1040 ... line 15, is zero or less') and takes the worksheet's own condition for Form 4952 filers (amb.2025.sd4952_selection), where the second follows Schedule D line 20 (sd.line20 false sends every Form 4952 filer with line 17 yes to the worksheet). Neither difference changes the tax: with line 4g and Schedule D lines 18 and 19 zero the Schedule D Tax Worksheet reduces to the other worksheet; with line 15 zero all three methods give zero; without qualified dividends or net capital gain qdcg.line25 is the tax on line 15; and line 4g above zero needs an amount on Form 4952 line 4b or 4e (f4952.bad_election refuses more). Checked by evaluating 233 non-refused returns (random wages, short- and long-term sales, qualified dividends, capital gain distributions, Form 4952 interest and elections, single and mfs) against the second's choice between sdtw.line47 and qdcg.line25: no difference, including 9 returns with line 15 above zero, Form 4952 filed, line 4g zero and Schedule D line 17 yes, and 25 with line 15 zero.

Ruling: representation; project retained. The election is for a social security benefit payment for an earlier year, so it can only apply to a filer with benefits; the project tests benefits first (the 'all' stops there) so a filer without benefits is never asked the lump-sum question, and for a filer with benefits the box is the answer itself.
